summary.title: Reverse Interviewing—How to interview a company as well as they interview you
summary.one_liner: You learn how to flip the interview, using a self-derived set of non-negotiables, themed reverse-interview questions, and back-channel references to evaluate a company before accepting a job.
keywords: questions to ask before accepting a job
takeaways: Reverse interview after you have an offer negotiated, but use softer signals during the formal process.
Define your non-negotiables and a flexible personal PMF first, then craft questions around them.
Group questions by theme (culture, strategy, role, goal-setting, communication) and ask the people best placed to answer.
Ask your future manager for three direct reports from prior roles; refusal is a red flag.
Push for specific examples; vague or hypothetical answers suggest a lack of truthfulness.
summary.summary: This is Part 2 of a three-part newsletter series by Adam Fishman on joining a new company. It explains what a reverse interview is and why to run one, then walks through the Company Evaluation Bullseye: identifying non-negotiables and a personal PMF using the Five Whys, then organizing questions by theme and by who should answer them. It shares sample reverse-interview questions contributed by named operators from companies such as Tile, Contentful, Reforge, and Thumbtack. The post also covers back-channel reference checks, including follow-up questions for former managers and colleagues, and closes with an anecdote about Zimride and Lyft.
